Which institutions and offices belong to the parliament and which to the government? Assign.
Select the correct answer. Only one answer is correct.

atoms.a: Who is responsible for passing new laws?
b: ++Parliament
the government
the prime minister
the cabinet

atoms.a: How are the winners determined in general elections?
b: ++A candidate needs the most overall votes to win.
A candidate needs more than 50% of the votes to win.
If no candidate gains more than 50% of the votes, there can be multiple winners.
The candidate of the leading party wins.

atoms.a: Who do British citizens vote for in general elections?
b: ++MPs representing their constituency in the House of Commons.
The new prime minister.
New members of the House of Lords.
Senior ministers in the cabinet.

atoms.a: How often do general elections normally take place?
b: ++every 5 years
every 4 years
every 2 years
every 8 years

atoms.a: How are members of the cabinet appointed?
b: They are democratically elected by citizens.
They are democratically elected by the leading party.
++They are chosen by the prime minister.
They are chosen by the House of Lords.

atoms.a: The UK is a constitutional monarchy. What does that mean?
b: ++The monarchy is only ceremonial; the real power lies with the government and Parliament.
The monarch has written a constitution that the government must follow.
The monarch is also the prime minister.
The constitution does not apply to the monarch.

atoms.a: The British constitution is not codified. What does “not codified” mean?
b: ++It has never been written down into one single document.
It has been amended many times.
It was not written by a monarch.
It cannot be amended without Parliament's consent.

atoms.a: What happens if the government or Parliament are dissolved?
b: ++New general elections must be held and everyone but the life peers are replaced.
The prime minister chooses the next government.
Only the MPs will be voted in anew, everyone else retains their office.
Parliament stays the same, but a new prime minister is elected.
